title: Regional fanout with backpressure valves and SLO-budgeted load-shedding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: the hosted API edge currently treats regions as independent endpoints with simple priority-based failover. For active-active traffic steering we need a coordinated approach that preserves SLOs during bursts and regional degradations, and that handles long-lived streaming sessions without causing loud user-visible truncation or token duplication.

Goal: Add a region-level fanout controller + backpressure valve system that coordinates per-region SLO budgets, exposes graceful degradation modes, and integrates with circuit attenuation and load-shedding policies. This should work for both request/response and streaming flows, preserve session continuity where possible, and provide clear observability for SLO burn and regional breathing windows.

High-level design:
- Fanout controller: gateway consults a lightweight region-policy store (cache) that contains per-region SLO budgets, current burn rates, and valve state (open/throttle/bypass). A request is routed to the preferred region if valve=open; if throttle, the gateway applies controlled shedding or reroutes according to policy.
- SLO-budget ledger: per-tenant and per-model ledger tracking token/latency budget consumption across regions for the rolling SLO window. Budget burn rate drives valve state transitions (normal -> throttle -> closed).
- Backpressure valves & regional breather windows: valves implement a token-bucket style allowance with exponential backoff on sustained burn. When closed, valve offers a short breather window (region enters "breather") and upstream traffic is preferentially shifted to other regions according to weighted capacity.
- Circuit attenuation: circuits trip at region or model granularity based on sustained SLO breach and infra saturation metrics. Attenuation reduces offered concurrency and applies a progressive shedding policy before total cutoff.
- Streaming considerations: streaming sessions are proxied through a lightweight session-relay that attaches a short-lived SPR (session-preserving reroute) token to the stream. If a stream needs to be moved between regions, the SPR token allows the new region's edge to rehydrate minimal session state (KV cache pointers + last-offset) and continue streaming without full replay. Reroutes try soft-degrade (throttle update frequency) before forcing reconnect.
- KV cache and prefix consistency: blurry reads are acceptable for short breather windows; critical prefixes (auth, session anchor) are strongly invalidated during reroutes.
- Observability & control: new dashboards: per-region SLO burn-rate, valve state timeline, streaming-stall ratio, SPR token rehydrate success/failure, and egress ripcord count. Expose telemetry to Console for per-route and per-tenant breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway can consult region-policy cache and make per-request routing decisions based on valve state
SLO-budget ledger records per-tenant/model token and latency consumption across regions with <5s propagation to policy cache
Valves transition through open->throttle->closed based on configurable burn thresholds and protected by exponential breather windows
Streaming session-relay implements SPR tokens and enables at least 90% successful soft-reroutes (state rehydrate) in staging under simulated region breather
Circuit attenuation reduces offered concurrency gradually and triggers alerts + dashboard updates (no silent blackholes), and documented rollback playbook exists
Playbook & canary: incremental rollout plan with canary rules, metrics guardrails (SLO burn, 99th latency, streaming-stall ratio), and automated rollback toggle
comments: 2026-02-16 | Aisha Kapoor: Initial spike complete. Proof-of-concept for policy cache + valve state machine implemented in proxy shim. Found that policy propagation latency from control-plane was too high (avg 8s) — need cache warm path and push invalidations for close/restore events.

2026-02-22 | Evelyn Chen: Decided to implement SLO-budget ledger in runtime telemetry service instead of gateway to avoid coupling. Ledger exposes a compact view to the policy cache via push subscription. Created RFC doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Fanout+and+Valve+RFC

2026-02-28 | Eng infra: Load test (simulating EU outage) shows valve backoff helps downstream region maintain 95th latency but increases 95th in alternate region by 12%. Trade-off noted — will add weighted fallback to avoid pushing single region to saturation.
2026-03-03 | Design review (Tomás Rivera): Suggested adding explicit UX labels in Console for "breather" vs "circuit-attenuated" to avoid operator confusion. Created design ticket DES-402.
2026-03-05 | PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1789 implements valve cache and routing hook. Needs unit tests and policy cache invalidation tests.

2026-03-09 | QA: Streaming soft-reroute test flaked under high concurrent KV cache misses. Mitigation: allow stashing of last-output-chunk in session-relay to reduce cold rehydrate penalty. Follow-up ENG-642802 created for stash storage API.
2026-03-10 | Evelyn Chen: Marking In Progress. Blockers: infra quota for multi-region load tests (ticket INFRA-231). Working with infra to get temporary quota increase for canary window.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive shedding keeps global SLOs but risks more 429s for individual tenants — mitigation is to make shedding per-tenant and to expose opt-out for high-tier customers
Security: SPR tokens are short-lived and HMAC-signed; we must run security review if we expand token scope (currently scoped to session rehydrate only)
Rollout plan: feature flag at route level, 3% global canary -> 10% regional canary -> 50% -> 100%. Monitor SLO burn + streaming-stall ratio at each step

Related artifacts: RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Fanout+and+Valve+RFC, Load-test results: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/region-fanout/stress-2026-02-28, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1789
